I’m eager to gain hackathon experience, contribute meaningfully, and collaborate with motivated teammates to build creative and impactful solutions.
summary:
Trail of Debris is a retro arcade detective game that turns 24 real NASA Mars and Moon missions into case files to solve. Players act as mission investigators. For each spacecraft that went silent, they inspect a clickable hardware blueprint, collect clues from engineering records, play a short mini-game based on the actual failure (balancing Apollo 13’s 15-amp power budget, converting Mars Climate Orbiter’s mixed-up units, tuning a radio to catch a faint signal), and then pick the hypothesis that explains what happened. A debrief shows the real outcome and what NASA learned from it.

This answers the “Abandoned But Not Forgotten” challenge by giving forgotten missions a second life as stories people play, not just read. Every case follows documented NASA history and never invents causes. Each case is written at three levels, for school students, college analysts and researchers. HELIX-7, an original 3D guide droid, gives hints along the way, and progress saves to the cloud.

It matters because failures teach as much as successes. Trail of Debris keeps those lessons alive and turns the next generation into engineers who ask “why?”
details:
What it does:

- A detective game about 24 real NASA Mars and Moon missions that went silent.

- You inspect the spacecraft's hardware, play a mini-game based on the real failure, and decide what caused it.

- A debrief then reveals what actually happened and what NASA learned.

Why it matters:

- Failures teach as much as successes, but most people only remember the headlines.

- Students become the investigators, sorting real evidence from guesses.

- Every case comes from documented NASA history. We never make up causes.

How we built it:

- Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

- three.js for our 3D guide droid, HELIX-7.

- The Web Audio API for 8-bit sounds.

- Supabase for cloud saves.

- Hosted free on GitHub Pages, so it plays in any browser with nothing to install.

What makes it different:

- Each mini-game is the real failure, like fixing Mars Climate Orbiter's unit mix-up or balancing Apollo 13's power budget.

- Every case comes in three difficulty levels, so a student and a researcher can play the same mission.

What we kept in mind:

- Accuracy: clues are marked "confirmed" or "suspected".

- Accessibility: high-contrast mode, reduced motion, and a sound toggle.

- Privacy: no sign-up and no personal data.

- Light enough to run on school computers.
